text:
The Stars arrived in Dallas on a five-game winning streak, and New Jersey ended it in a hurry. The Devils won 5-1, their fourth straight, and Nico Hischier, the first overall pick in 2017, supplied two of the goals, both snap shots, one in the first period and one 38 seconds into the second. That second period belonged to New Jersey. By its end the Devils led 4-1, with Jesper Boqvist adding a wrist shot from a chance our model gave only a 6% shot of going in.

The numbers say the Devils were better, though not by as much as the score suggests. On expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, New Jersey led 2.8 to 1.71 and took 60 shot attempts to Dallas's 38. At even strength, though, the gap was narrow: 1.47 to 1.69, with Dallas slightly ahead. Our simulation of the game, replaying every shot, gave New Jersey a 70% chance to win. Casey DeSmith allowed 2.2 goals more than his workload deserved, while Connor Hellebuyck stopped 17 of 18 shots and finished 0.71 goals ahead of what the chances called for. The Stars also took 21 penalty minutes to New Jersey's 5, though the Devils went 0 for 3 on the power play.

Justin Hryckowian's tip-in at 16:08 of the second briefly cut it to 3-1, but Luke Hughes restored the margin 28 seconds later, and Jack Hughes, who led all skaters with six shots on goal, closed the scoring in the third. Dallas now has to start a new streak. New Jersey has four wins in a row, and the three stars were its first line and defense: Hischier, Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes.
